evidence: Read every criterion description in all five dimensions (40 functional, 5 polish, 5 visual, 2 gates = 52) looking for the workbook defect: a list of requirements followed by a waiver of most of them, leaving two targets. None found. Every binary criterion states its bar and then a 'Fails if ...' list that restates the same bar, closed by the uniform 'Fails if any condition stated above does not hold.' The relaxations present are single-target conditionals or alternative implementations, each consistent with hireops_rules.md, not waivers of enumerated requirements: (a) hro_job_open (functional judge.toml:29) 'the team, manager and places are shown wherever the app shows job details or are evidenced by behaviour' - rules s2 requires a job to HAVE a team/manager/places but does not require staff display, so the bar is one target: entered values correct wherever shown; refusals of blank title/0/51/2.5/non-manager all remain required. (b) hro_add_candidate (:38) email/source 'wherever the app shows card details' - same conditional pattern, explicit fail 'shows wrong details'. (c) 'whether tried through the UI or, if not offered, by replay; hiding it is optional' (hro_move_one_stage :56, hro_reject_hired :92, hro_mgr_other_job :164) and 'Whether the Observer's screens show such controls is the app's choice' (:173), 'Whether the undo control is hidden is the app's choice' (:254) - matches functional prompt.md:23 ('what is graded is that the server refuses it'); one bar (server refusal, nothing changes). (d) hro_refused_put_back (:137) 'A UI that refuses before the card moves ... also passes' still requires reason shown and focus on the card - alternative implementation, same bar. (e) hro_reject_reason (:83) reason/rejected-from 'on the card, its details, its reopen control or its Activity line' - placement freedom, one bar. (f) hro_activity (:263) 'one line naming every card of a multi-card move with its stages also satisfies that move' - alternative format, no waiver. (g) Ownership hand-offs (hro_arrive_bottom :65, hro_interview_full :110, hro_drafts :371, hro_candidate_view :380, hro_candidate_linked :398, hro_pol_live_thread :32, hro_pol_failed_send :50) move a sub-observable to a named sibling instead of waiving it; this is anti-double-deduction scoping, not a second target. (h) Polish hro_pol_session_resume (:59) 'unless the sign-in prompt has already appeared on its own (that also passes)' matches rules s6 Drafts ('as soon as the workspace notices, at the latest on the next action'). Visual likert rows have one dimension each with 5 described anchors; gates state one bar each ('a refusal message is welcome but not required' in hro_gate_render is consistent with its fail condition). Per SKILL.md Known false positives and the internal annotation, conjunctive whole-flow criteria (e.g. hro_mgr_early_refused, hro_undo_conflict, hro_candidate_private) are not check-33 defects. Adversarial probes: broken app storing a wrong team but never showing it on staff screens - still caught where the team is shown (candidate view, rules s7, hro_candidate_view); conforming app that shows no manager on screen - passes hro_job_open via behaviour in R. Minor, non-blocking wording observations (Note-level, P3, no second target established): (1) hro_candidate_private (:389) bans 'board positions' in any candidate response yet allows board/Activity replays 'answered with only that candidate's own data'; a lenient judge could read own-card position as 'own data', but the explicit forbidden list in the same sentence and rules s7 ('a card's place on the board') resolve it to one bar. (2) hro_pol_live_board (polish :23) 'add cards until one does, or record that no scroll exists and judge the other legs' leaves slight judge discretion over when the scroll leg is waived; it is a defined fallback, not a waiver of enumerated requirements. (3) hro_job_open's 'evidenced by behaviour (the manager's own moves in R ...)' could, for an app that never displays the manager and whose R moves fail, couple the defect into a second row; prompt.md:23 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row' governs. This is a static textual check; no runtime evidence is required for it, and no Oracle/model/portal result is implied.
